motion.why: 2026-11-05 (Mike: move as the motors really can, generous S-shaped speed-up / slow-down so nothing wobbles or skips). Joint output speeds deg/s and accelerations deg/s^2. A NEMA 17 keeps ~0.40 N.m at ~300 rpm (24 V, 2 A) = 48.6 deg/s through the 37:1 drive; loaded joints run well under that. Swivel: 4:1 bevel, limited by the arm's inertia (wobble), not torque. | 2026-11-05 (Mike: push the cruise rpm): tools/motor_speed.py - pull-out torque at 24 V vs the worst gravity load anywhere on the board, x1.5 margin, printed-cycloid input capped at 600 rpm until bench-tested: J2 80 deg/s (493 rpm), J3 / J4 95 (586 rpm), J1 45 (277 rpm: its margin at full reach is only x1.13 at ANY speed and the 60 mm motor's coil figures are estimated), swivel 90 (60 rpm at the motor; its ramps, not the motor, limit it). Accelerations unchanged. Measured on the seed-5 game: cruise alone buys ~0.1 min - the moves are short and J1's acceleration sets the pace.

arm_note: 2026-11-05: tube links (mockup_link.py) on spread gearboxes, base arm_tube.py, claw claw_adapter.py --spread; the box-link arm is in scene_boxlink_backup.json
motors_note: 2026-11-05 (Mike): J1 60 mm (73 N.cm), J2 48, J3 48, J4 23 mm pancake (15.5 N.cm), swivel 48

bowden.why: 2026-11-05 (Mike): the claw's Bowden (PTFE 4 x 2) in the arm's plane along the OUTSIDE of the arch: straight up out of the claw adapter's 16 mm bore, up along link C's outside, a wide arc over the J3 knuckle (72 from its axis, clear of everything there, which reaches 54), down onto the back of link B into the servo's guide - the servo tilted 30 deg outward so the tube leaves already curving into the arc (servo spot is a placeholder until its mount is designed). The servo sits on link B by J2 in a 30 deg mount glued into two D16 side holes (servo_tube.py). Cubic Bezier chain through the anchors (p in the anchor's joint frame, d = tube direction, k = handle share); tuned so the tightest bend over the whole demo is r ~54 (PTFE min ~30). Length 452..541 mm over the demo.
